scope: Two missing military war resisters after return from Canada; distinguish actual US jail time from exile and preserve unresolved dates.

ryan2016.label: Laura Kaminker, War resister Ryan Johnson needs our help, October 15, 2016; personal acquaintance and War Resisters Support Campaign organizer confirms actual imprisonment and ten-month sentence.

ryan2017.label: Courage to Resist, March 23, 2017, Support Ryan Johnson, Imprisoned War Resister; brig correspondence, family visits, IVAW organizing and still-prospective May release.

ryan-release.label: Jeff Paterson for Courage to Resist, October 5, 2017 fundraising update reproduced October 6 by American Left History; explicit actual release and resettlement in Denver. Original HTML retrieved.

hart2011.label: Bruce Beyer statement of March 27, 2011 and contemporary support notice reproduced by Adopt Resistance; Patrick Brendan Hart in Christian County Jail after a 25-month sentence.

hart-history.label: Luke Stewart, Active History, November 2012, The re-writing of history; Patrick Hart returned voluntarily and was sentenced to 25 months. April 2011 timing conflicts with March contemporary notice.

hart-release.label: Carolyn Thompson/AP, July 12, 2015, War resisters finding no refuge in Canada, San Antonio Express-News; used for actual completed imprisonment and release, not an exact verified endpoint.

prisoner.name: Ryan Johnson
prisoner.description: Ryan Johnson was a US Army soldier who refused deployment to Iraq and sought refuge in Canada. He helped organize a Toronto chapter of Iraq Veterans Against the War before returning to the United States and serving a military prison term.

cases.charges: Military prosecution following unauthorized absence and refusal of Iraq deployment; exact plea specifications unverified
cases.sentence: A supporter reported his court-martial, ten-month sentence and actual imprisonment in October 2016. A March 2017 campaign update describes continuing confinement at Miramar and visits from his wife. An October 2017 report confirms release and resettlement. The earlier predicted May release is not entered as an actual date.

case_research.custody_evidence: A personal acquaintance confirms imprisonment in 2016; subsequent brig letters and visits establish continued custody in 2017; the support organization then confirms release.

entries.custody_evidence: A personal acquaintance confirms imprisonment in 2016; subsequent brig letters and visits establish continued custody in 2017; the support organization then confirms release.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Ten months is the imposed sentence, not verified actual time served. Year-only endpoints prevent a fabricated exact counter. His eleven years in Canada are not counted as US imprisonment. IVAW chapter organizing is explicitly documented. Exact statutory plea, birth/death dates, individual custody days and portrait reuse attribution remain unresolved. Do not use photographs or birthdays of sporting or criminal namesakes.

prisoner.name: Patrick Brendan Hart
prisoner.description: Patrick Hart was a US Army sergeant who publicly opposed the Iraq War while seeking refuge in Canada. He later returned voluntarily and was imprisoned following military prosecution for his refusal to deploy.

cases.charges: Desertion following refusal of Iraq deployment
cases.sentence: A March 27, 2011 support notice identifies him in Christian County Jail after sentencing the previous week to twenty-five months. Later reporting confirms completed military imprisonment and release. Conflicting chronology prevents entering a reliable release date or actual total served. Military discharge is separate from jail release.

case_research.custody_evidence: A contemporary named prison-support notice follows sentencing; the subsequent interview confirms that he actually served time and was released.

entries.custody_evidence: A contemporary named prison-support notice follows sentencing; the subsequent interview confirms that he actually served time and was released.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Contemporary March 27 notice precedes the April 2011 sentencing cited in a later history, so March precision is used without inventing a day. The later press report gives release in 2013 after 15 months, which is difficult to reconcile with March 2011 imprisonment; both endpoint and documented-month field are withheld pending better records. Subsequent freedom supports released=true. His Canadian exile is not imprisonment. Expanded name from the prison notice was checked against aliases; unrelated UK climate activist Dr Patrick Hart, the monk, and military namesakes are excluded. Formal IVAW membership not inferred.
